title: The Deadliest Kick in Africa Belongs to a Bird, and It Lasts 15 Milliseconds

scenes.text: The deadliest kick in Africa belongs to a bird.
The secretary bird stands over a metre tall, with the longest legs of any raptor.
It walks twenty to thirty kilometres a day, hunting snakes. Including cobras.
scenes.keywords: secretary bird hunting cobra snake grass

scenes.text: Scientists trained one named Madeleine to stomp a rubber snake laid over a force plate.
scenes.keywords: secretary bird stomping bird of prey trainer

scenes.text: Each kick hit with 195 newtons, five times its body weight, and lasted just fifteen milliseconds.
scenes.keywords: secretary bird kicking snake slow motion

scenes.text: That's a tenth of an eye blink, far too fast for a snake to answer. Africa's deadliest kick, on two skinny legs.

description:
The secretary bird kills snakes, including cobras, with a kick that hits with about 195 newtons, roughly five times its body weight, and lasts only about 15 milliseconds, a tenth of an eye blink.
Researchers measured it in 2016 (Portugal et al., Current Biology) by training a captive bird named Madeleine at the Hawk Conservancy Trust to strike a rubber snake over a force plate. It stands up to 1.3 metres tall and walks 20 to 30 kilometres a day.
Which bird would win in a kicking contest?
subject: secretary bird
first_comment: Madeleine is actually a male; the keepers named him before they knew. Which animal has the most underrated weapon?
